panels.title: Quantum-vulnerable frames accepted by the CLOUD
panels.description: The migration's success indicator. Scoped to the cloud on purpose: the cloud is the node we control end to end, so any non-zero value here means quantum-vulnerable traffic got all the way in. A cumulative counter is right for this question - 'has this EVER happened' - because one accepted frame is already a problem. Stays at 0 once the gateway speaks the post-quantum suite.

panels.title: Last-mile exposure at the GATEWAY (expected)
panels.description: Legacy frames the gateway accepts from the device. This is NOT a failure and will never reach zero: the device is frozen firmware that can only speak the legacy suite, so brokering means the gateway must accept it. Tracking it separately is the point - it quantifies the residual risk the migration does not remove. See docs/risks.md R1.

panels.title: Suite in use per link
panels.description: Configured posture of every link. quantum_resistant=false on the device link is the architecture working as designed, not a misconfiguration.

panels.title: Vulnerable frame rate, by service
panels.description: Rate rather than cumulative total, so this answers 'is it happening right now'. The gateway line should be steady while the device transmits; the cloud line should sit flat on zero. If the cloud line ever lifts, the migration has regressed.

panels.title: Frames accepted by the cloud, by suite
panels.description: After migration this should be entirely post-quantum.

panels.title: Handshake duration p95 by suite
panels.description: ML-KEM decapsulation is cheaper than RSA decryption, but the hybrid handshake does more work overall on the initiator.

panels.title: Frame outcomes
panels.description: A rise in rejected frames during a migration usually means a suite mismatch rather than an attack.
